result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): B is the denser, easier-to-scan queue. All eight tickets are visible, the current row has an outline as well as a background tint, and a footer lists every shortcut, including undo. A also shows undo, but expanding the selected row pushes tickets out of view, and the green border around the whole list makes it less clear which row is current. The screenshots can't show motion, empty states or narrow widths, so those scores are inferred and roughly even. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): A fits all eight tickets in a dense, scannable list. The current row is marked by a full outline as well as a background change, so it doesn't rely on color alone, and a persistent footer lists the shortcuts, including undo. B has nice detail and also shows undo, but expanding the selected row pushes the list past the viewport so only about six tickets are visible, and its focus ring around the whole list makes the current row less distinct. Items 2–5 can't be checked from static screenshots, so those scores are neutral guesses based on the visible undo controls.
